clue.text: Carry out punt for an older woman

parts.note: to carry out a task is to do it
a punt is a bet, a wager

explanation.surface: Someone takes a boat out on the river for an elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' suggests the flat-bottomed boat, but here it is the British slang for a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title from her late husband, typically an elderly lady of standing.

clue.text: Innovative lines in underwear not at all sensible

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside another

parts.note: bras are items of underwear

indicators.note: something innovative is newly devised, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new design of lingerie is judged to be foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innovative' turns LINES into INLES, which goes 'in' BRAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no brain is witless, lacking all sense.

clue.text: … when a man of science wants up-to the-minute style

parts.note: up-to-the-minute means new
ton is an old word for fashionable style

explanation.surface: A scientist hopes to look fashionable and modern.
explanation.walkthrough: Isaac Newton, the physicist; the clue's leading ellipsis carries on from the previous clue in the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton is the celebrated English physicist and mathematician, an example of a scientist.

clue.text: When the weather's fine a painter spends less time at home

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
in means at home
taken as written

explanation.surface: In good weather an artist stays out of the house more.
explanation.definitionFit: A day with no rain is one of fair, dry weather.

clue.text: Protests to do with awards

parts.note: re means concerning, to do with
presentations are the handing over of awards

explanation.surface: Complaints are raised about prize-givings.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal representations are statements of complaint or objection made to an authority.

clue.text: Annoyed about kit getting wet

indicators.note: about says one word wraps round the other

parts.note: irate means annoyed
rig is equipment, kit

explanation.surface: Someone is cross that their gear got soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate land is to supply it with water.

clue.text: Left a quarter, no less!

parts.note: east is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: An exclamation that someone departed with fully a quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: 'At least' means no less than the amount given, the minimum.

clue.text: Rickets troubled this artist

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A painter suffered from a childhood bone disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Sickert was an English painter of the Camden Town Group.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Sickert is a British painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: The way people scoff!

definitions.meaning: a ... of a meal is what diners eat greedily

explanation.definitionFit: A course is both a direction taken and one stage of a meal that people devour.

clue.text: It appears normal to cut the talk

parts.note: par is the normal level
to lance is to cut open

explanation.surface: Ordinary people seem to interrupt the conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular manner of speaking, the idiom or jargon used.

clue.text: Case of wine sent back by college head

indicators.note: head of college means its first letter
sent back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine

explanation.surface: A college principal returns a crate of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a metal container, a kind of case.

clue.text: Infer this is the weapon of a woman

parts.note: gat is slang for a gun
her refers to something belonging to a woman

explanation.surface: Someone deduces that a weapon belongs to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather from evidence is to conclude, deduce.

clue.text: May be licensed to manufacture sinks

indicators.note: to manufacture is to make up, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A firm might have permission to make kitchen sinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that declines goes down, falls or sinks.

clue.text: Being without serving men from first to last

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: an entity is a being
RE is the Royal Engineers, soldiers in service

explanation.surface: A person existing with no servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking', but here it is the old sense 'outside'; RE, the Royal Engineers, are British Army soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole of something runs complete, beginning to end.

clue.text: Prompter to accept a surplus

indicators.note: to accept here means to take in, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: a reminder prompts someone's memory

explanation.surface: A theatre prompter agrees to an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A remainder is what is left over, the excess.

clue.text: Craftsman after a little cash — irregular

indicators.note: after puts the craftsman piece later than the cash

parts.note: p is a penny, a small amount of money
an artisan is a skilled craftsman

explanation.surface: A craftsman is chasing a small sum of money, but irregularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' as a noun means a guerrilla fighter, not a regular soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a guerrilla, a fighter outside the regular army.

clue.text: Firm not favouring a high-minded individual, a hard worker

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
ST is a saint, someone of high virtue
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A company opposes an idealist who works hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and steady both describe something unchanging.

clue.text: Bunting many put up in a foreign port

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Oran is a port in Algeria

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means written bottom to top

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: Lots of decorative bunting is hung in an overseas harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunting' suggests flags; it is the bird family.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small Eurasian bird of the bunting family.

clue.text: Twisted to get a fix

definitions.meaning: turned in a spiral, like a thread
to be victim of a fix, cheated or swindled

explanation.definitionFit: Screwed means turned with a twist and, in slang, cheated by a rigged deal.

clue.text: A nice arrangement after all — so compact

indicators.note: after places the rearranged piece behind all

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A tidy set-up is so neat, after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges A NICE into IANCE; 'compact' is the noun meaning a pact, not the adjective meaning small.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact is an agreement between parties, a pact or league.

clue.text: Find in Hilaire Belloc a teller of good tales

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Hilaire Belloc was a storyteller of fine tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilaire Belloc wrote Cautionary Tales; the answer runs across 'Belloc a teller'.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something is to discover where it is, to pinpoint its position.

clue.text: Brood about trade recession when hard-pressed

indicators.note: about says one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a hen sits on eggs to brood

indicators.note: recession means going back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: art means a craft or trade

explanation.surface: A trader worries about an economic downturn while under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' reverses ART into TRA; 'strait' as an adjective is old-fashioned for tight or distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Strait as an adjective means constricted or in difficulties, as in dire straits.

clue.text: A woman bringing up five in the Italian capital

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another
bringing up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: the lira was Italy's money, its capital
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A lady takes five children to Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like Rome; it is money, the old Italian lira, turned upward to ARIL with V inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Avril is a female forename, an example of a woman.

clue.text: Smoke in church and a large number will be furious

parts.note: incense is burnt to give fragrant smoke in church
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A congregation will be angry at smoke filling the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Incensed means made extremely angry, enraged.

clue.text: Clears of pollution in the open air

indicators.note: pollution spoils and muddles things, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The air outdoors is cleaned of pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco is an Italian loan phrase meaning outdoors.

clue.text: Cover for the brave with dependants

definitions.text: Cover for the brave with dependants

parts.words: Cover for the brave with dependants
parts.note: a Native American warrior's shelter where his family live too

explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent used as a home by Plains peoples.

clue.text: Is disposed for the slopes

explanation.definitionFit: Inclines means both tends towards something and slants upward.
